overall: The AG found the Weymouth Town Council violated the Open Meeting Law by using its secretary to collect members' digital signatures on a letter, which constituted improper deliberation outside a noticed meeting; the Council was ordered to comply going forward.

allegations.summary: Council allegedly deliberated outside a noticed meeting by having its secretary gather members' digital signatures on a letter to the Mayor and a developer.
allegations.key_passage: The Council violated the Open Meeting Law by utilizing its secretary to gather the opinions of members for the purposes of sending the letter at issue.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law
Caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law
remedy_passage: We order the Council's immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and we caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
